entry.title: Typographical Symbols of Note
entry.content:
The manicule, ☞, is a typographical mark with the appearance of a hand with its index finger extended in a pointing gesture.

The silcrow, or section sign, (§) is a typographical symbol for referencing individually numbered sections of a document.

In typography, the pilcrow (¶) is a grapheme used to identify a paragraph.

A dagger, obelisk, or obelus † is a typographical mark that usually indicates a footnote if an asterisk has already been used.

A fleuron, ❦, also known as a printers' flower, is a typographical symbol, or glyph, used either as a punctuation mark or as an ornament for typographic compositions.

entry.title: Drop Shadows
entry.content: Due to its importance in our lives, the sun is most often depicted in illustrations to the upper left — the most prominent placement possible. Therefore, drop shadows should reflect this by being placed to the lower right.

entry.title: The Accident of My Birthday
entry.content:
I was born, fortuitously, at one second past midnight on January the first in the year 1800. Thus, my age has always reflected the year. This was as true in the 19th century as it is in the current 21st century.

I bring this up because it may be a clue. For it was at one second past midnight on the day I turned 26 that I suddenly found myself exactly 200 years into the future.

I’m not sure what to make of it, but I am convinced that the marvelous new technologies of this era may aid me. This web log is an experimentation to that end.
